title: Class D vs. Untowered Airports
subtitle: Majors Field Class D, Class E vignettes, private fields and obstructions
keyTakeaway: Dashed blue = Class D up to the bracketed MSL ceiling and needs authorization. A fuzzy magenta ring means Class E starts at 700 ft AGL, so the drone layer below it is Class G.

hotspots.title: Majors (GVT) Class D [30]
hotspots.summary: Majors Airport at Greenville has a blue airport symbol (part-time control tower — check star/Chart Supplement for effective hours) and a dashed blue Class D boundary. The [30] box means the Class D ceiling is 3,000 ft MSL. Field elevation is 535 ft and the longest runway is 8,000 ft (L 80). A parachute symbol sits just north-northeast of the runway symbol.
hotspots.examTrap: The bracketed number is an MSL ceiling in hundreds of feet, not AGL. 3,000 MSL over a 535 ft field is only about 2,465 ft AGL.

hotspots.title: Sulphur Springs Municipal (SLR)
hotspots.summary: Magenta airport symbol = no control tower. The star on top marks a rotating beacon. Data block "489 L 50 123.075 C": field elevation 489 ft MSL, runway lighting, longest runway 5,000 ft, and 123.075 is the CTAF (the circled C). The fuzzy magenta vignette around the field means Class E begins at 700 ft AGL.
hotspots.examTrap: The AWOS frequency (118.35) is for weather only. Traffic advisories go on the CTAF, 123.075.

hotspots.title: Commerce (2F7) Class E 700 ft Vignette
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: The fuzzy magenta ring around Commerce Municipal marks where Class E drops to 700 ft AGL. From the surface up to 700 ft AGL it is Class G, so a drone at 400 ft AGL needs no ATC authorization. Field elevation 516 ft, 3,900 ft runway, CTAF 122.9.
hotspots.examTrap: Fuzzy (shaded) magenta = Class E floor at 700 AGL. Dashed magenta = Class E down to the surface. Only the dashed version needs authorization.

hotspots.title: Area 5: Hidden Springs (Pvt)
hotspots.summary: Area 5 marks Hidden Springs, a magenta "R" in a circle labeled (Pvt) with "485 - 25": a private, non-public-use field at 485 ft MSL with a 2,500 ft runway.
hotspots.examTrap: The circled R is a private airport, not a restricted area. Restricted areas are blue hatched boundaries labeled R-xxxx.

hotspots.title: Group Obstruction 1009 (460)
hotspots.summary: North of Greenville (note: Figure 24 is oriented with north to the left of the page), the double-peak symbol is a group obstruction. The bold italic 1009 is the top of the obstruction in feet MSL; (460) in parentheses is its height above ground.
hotspots.examTrap: The parenthesized number is AGL. Don't subtract it from the MSL figure; that gives you the ground elevation, not the height.

title: Class C: Surface Area and Shelf
subtitle: Toledo Class C, a Detroit Class B shelf, a tall tower and a Class E surface area
keyTakeaway: Solid magenta = Class C. The inner ring (xx/SFC) needs authorization from the ground up; under the outer shelf (xx/20) a 400 ft drone is still below Class C.

hotspots.title: Toledo Express (TOL) Class C Surface Area
hotspots.summary: The inner solid magenta circle around Toledo Express is labeled 47/SFC: Class C from the surface to 4,700 ft MSL. Field elevation 683 ft, longest runway 10,600 ft (L 106).
hotspots.examTrap: Class C altitudes are MSL. 4,700 MSL over a 683 ft field is about 4,000 ft AGL.

hotspots.title: Toledo Class C Outer Shelf 47/20
hotspots.summary: Between the inner and outer magenta circles, 47/20 means Class C from 2,000 ft MSL to 4,700 ft MSL. Ground here is roughly 600 to 700 ft MSL, so the shelf starts about 1,300 ft above the ground.
hotspots.examTrap: A drone at 400 ft AGL under the 47/20 shelf is below Class C. Authorization depends on the airspace underneath, not the shelf.

hotspots.title: Detroit Class B Shelf 100/40
hotspots.summary: Solid blue lines near Monroe are the Detroit Class B. The 100/40 label means this shelf runs from 4,000 ft MSL to 10,000 ft MSL. Farther north the 100/30 shelf starts at 3,000 ft MSL.
hotspots.examTrap: Class B is solid blue; Class D is dashed blue. Don't confuse the two line styles.

hotspots.title: Lighted Tower 1817 (1090)
hotspots.summary: South of Deshler, the tall tower symbol with lightning-flash marks is a high-intensity lighted obstruction. 1817 is the top in feet MSL; (1090) is its height above ground. The taller symbol is used for obstructions 1,000 ft AGL and higher.
hotspots.examTrap: The flash marks mean high-intensity lights, not "under construction". UC is printed as letters next to the numbers.

hotspots.title: Findlay (FDY) Class E Surface Area
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Findlay Airport is magenta (no tower) and is enclosed by a dashed magenta line: Class E airspace starting at the surface. Field elevation 813 ft, 6,500 ft runway. Area 3 sits just west of it, near Mt Cory.
hotspots.examTrap: An untowered airport can still have controlled airspace to the surface. Dashed magenta means you need authorization even with no tower.

title: Class B: The Upside-Down Wedding Cake
subtitle: DFW Class B surface area, shelves, and Class D airports underneath
keyTakeaway: Each Class B shelf has its own MSL floor. Only the SFC core needs authorization from the ground; under higher shelves check what lies beneath.

hotspots.title: Area 5: DFW Class B Surface Area
hotspots.summary: Area 5 sits inside the 110/SFC core of the Dallas-Fort Worth Class B, next to DFW International (elevation 607 ft, longest runway 13,400 ft). "NO SVFR" means no special VFR for fixed-wing aircraft.
hotspots.examTrap: 110/SFC: the top number is the ceiling (11,000 ft MSL). SFC means the floor is the ground, so authorization is required at any altitude.

hotspots.title: Class B Shelf 110/20
hotspots.summary: Northeast of DFW (note: Figure 25 is oriented with north to the left), the 110/20 shelf runs from 2,000 ft MSL up to 11,000 ft MSL. Terrain is about 600 ft MSL, so the shelf begins roughly 1,400 ft above the ground. A drone at 400 ft AGL is below it.
hotspots.examTrap: The bottom number is MSL, not AGL. 20 = 2,000 ft MSL.

hotspots.title: Area 4: Hicks Airport (T67) under Class B
hotspots.summary: Hicks (T67) is magenta (no tower): elevation 855 ft, 3,700 ft runway, CTAF 123.05. It sits under a Class B shelf whose floor is 4,000 ft MSL. Fort Worth Meacham is to the southeast.
hotspots.examTrap: Classic FAA question: the floor of Class B over Hicks is 4,000 ft MSL, not the surface and not Meacham's 3,200 ft Class D ceiling.

hotspots.title: Fort Worth Meacham (FTW) Class D [32]
hotspots.summary: Meacham International has a dashed blue Class D ring with [32]: surface to 3,200 ft MSL. Field elevation 710 ft, 7,500 ft runway. The DFW Class B shelves sit above it.
hotspots.examTrap: [32] is 3,200 ft MSL. Above that, the Class B shelf takes over, not Class G.

hotspots.title: Denton Enterprise (DTO) Class D [25]
hotspots.summary: Denton Enterprise has a blue airport symbol and a dashed blue Class D marked [25]: surface to 2,500 ft MSL. Elevation 642 ft, 7,000 ft runway. Area 1 sits just north-northeast under the Class B shelf labeled 100/40 (floor 4,000 ft MSL).
hotspots.examTrap: 2,500 MSL minus 642 ft field elevation is only about 1,860 ft AGL.

title: Coastal Airspace: Norfolk & Elizabeth City
subtitle: Class C, part-time Class D, warning areas, hazards and wildlife refuges
keyTakeaway: Read the notes printed on the chart. Balloon cables, part-time towers and refuge altitude requests all show up as exam questions.

hotspots.title: Norfolk Intl Class C Surface Area (40/SFC)
hotspots.summary: Inside the inner magenta circle (40/SFC) around Norfolk International is Class C from the surface to 4,000 ft MSL (field elevation 27 ft, 9,000 ft runway). Note that Area 1 farther east lies outside the inner ring under the 40/12 outer shelf (1,200 ft MSL floor).
hotspots.examTrap: Inside the 40/SFC inner ring, ATC authorization is required from the surface up; under the outer 40/12 shelf, Class C starts at 1,200 ft MSL.

hotspots.title: Elizabeth City (ECG) Class D [25]
hotspots.summary: Elizabeth City CGAS/Regional sits inside a dashed blue Class D ring ([25] = 2,500 ft MSL; elevation 11 ft, 7,200 ft runway). The note "See NOTAMs/Directory for Class D/E (sfc) eff hrs" flags a part-time tower. Note that Area 3 farther east lies outside ECG's Class D inside Currituck's 700 ft Class E vignette (Class G at the surface).
hotspots.examTrap: When the ECG tower closes, its surface area normally reverts to Class E (still controlled), not Class G.

hotspots.title: Unmarked Balloon on Cable
hotspots.summary: Southeast of Elizabeth City the chart warns: "CAUTION: UNMARKED BALLOON ON CABLE TO 3008' MSL. CHECK NOTAMS." The tethered balloon and its cable are a collision hazard at drone altitudes.
hotspots.examTrap: The FAA asks what hazard lies about 4 SM southeast of ECG. It is the balloon, not the military operations note farther north.

hotspots.title: Warning Area W-50B
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: Off the Virginia Beach coast, blue hatched boundaries outline Warning Areas W-50A, W-50B and W-50C, with Restricted Area R-6606 near the shoreline. Warning areas lie beyond 3 NM from the coast and contain activity hazardous to nonparticipating aircraft.
hotspots.examTrap: Warning areas are not prohibited, but they can hold live-fire or other hazardous activity. Don't confuse W- with R- (restricted).

hotspots.title: Area 6: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
hotspots.ceiling: Pilots requested to stay above 2,000 ft AGL
hotspots.summary: Area 6 is at Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge, just north of Mackay Island NWR. Pilots are requested to maintain at least 2,000 ft AGL over charted refuges. Launching or landing a drone on refuge land is also restricted by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
hotspots.examTrap: The 2,000 ft AGL request is advisory for overflight. It does not make the refuge restricted airspace.

title: Minot Class D, Towers and MOAs
subtitle: Class D math, tall towers, Class E vignettes, refuges and a MOA
keyTakeaway: Subtract field elevation from MSL figures to get AGL. MOAs need no authorization, but watch for fast military traffic.

hotspots.title: Minot Intl (MOT) Class D [42]
hotspots.summary: Minot International is a blue towered airport in a dashed blue Class D ring marked [42]: surface to 4,200 ft MSL. Elevation 1,716 ft, 7,700 ft runway. Dashed magenta lines around it mark Class E surface extensions.
hotspots.examTrap: 4,200 ft MSL over a 1,716 ft field is only about 2,500 ft above the runway.

hotspots.title: Lighted Tower 3149 (1031)
hotspots.summary: South-southwest of Minot, a cluster of towers includes one charted 3149 (1031) with lightning-flash marks: 3,149 ft MSL, 1,031 ft above the ground, high-intensity lighted. A neighbor is 2879 (700) UC, under construction.
hotspots.examTrap: Pick the AGL figure in parentheses when asked how tall the tower is above the terrain.

hotspots.title: Garrison (D05) Class E 700 ft Vignette
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Garrison Municipal is magenta (no tower) with elevation 1,937 ft, a 3,700 ft lighted runway and CTAF 122.9. The fuzzy magenta ring means Class E starts at 700 ft AGL; below that is Class G.
hotspots.examTrap: The vignette lowers Class E to 700 AGL but does not reach the surface. No authorization needed at 400 AGL.

hotspots.title: Audubon National Wildlife Refuge
hotspots.ceiling: Pilots requested to stay above 2,000 ft AGL
hotspots.summary: The blue outline along Audubon Lake marks Audubon National Wildlife Refuge. Pilots are asked to stay at least 2,000 ft AGL, and drone takeoffs and landings on refuge land are restricted.
hotspots.examTrap: A refuge is not Special Use Airspace you need LAANC for; it is a noise-sensitive area with an altitude request.

hotspots.title: Devils Lake West MOA
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: The magenta hatched boundary on the east side is Devils Lake West MOA. A MOA separates military training from IFR traffic. VFR and drone operations are allowed without permission, but be alert for high-speed military aircraft.
hotspots.examTrap: MOAs do not require ATC authorization. Restricted areas do.

title: Restricted Areas, MOAs and Class E
subtitle: R-5401/R-5402, Devils Lake East MOA, Jamestown and Cooperstown
keyTakeaway: Blue hatched R- boundaries need permission from the using agency when active. Magenta hatched MOAs only need vigilance.

hotspots.title: Restricted Areas R-5401 / R-5402
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: The blue hatched circle is Restricted Area R-5402 with R-5401 inside it. The chart notes "R-5402 excludes airspace within R-5401 and R-5403A when active" and gives 1-800-972-8824 for R-5402 and R-5403 information.
hotspots.examTrap: Restricted areas need permission from the controlling or using agency, not LAANC.

hotspots.title: Devils Lake East MOA
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: Devils Lake East MOA is labeled in magenta with the note "MOA excludes airspace within restricted areas when active." Its magenta hatched boundary runs diagonally across the chart.
hotspots.examTrap: Where a MOA and restricted area overlap, the restricted area takes precedence when active.

hotspots.title: Area 2: Cooperstown (S32) Class E 700 ft
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Area 2 sits inside the fuzzy magenta ring around Cooperstown Municipal, so Class E begins at 700 ft AGL with Class G below. Cooperstown: elevation 1,424 ft, 3,500 ft lighted runway, CTAF 122.9.
hotspots.examTrap: Use the circled-C frequency (122.9) for traffic calls, not the AWOS frequency.

hotspots.title: Jamestown Regional (JMS) Class E Surface
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Jamestown Regional is magenta (no tower) with a dashed magenta Class E surface boundary. Elevation 1,500 ft, 6,500 ft runway, CTAF 123.0. Area 4, just north, sits on the magenta vignette that surrounds the airport.
hotspots.examTrap: No tower does not mean uncontrolled. The dashed magenta line makes this Class E down to the ground.

hotspots.title: Area 3: Class G near Courtenay
hotspots.summary: Area 3 has no magenta vignette or airport boundary nearby, so Class G extends from the surface to 1,200 ft AGL. Just south is an obstruction charted 1843 (299): 1,843 ft MSL, 299 ft AGL.
hotspots.examTrap: Away from vignettes, Class E usually starts at 1,200 ft AGL, not 700.

title: Mountain Airports & Seaplane Bases
subtitle: Part-time Class E, seaplane bases, MEFs and towers in high terrain
keyTakeaway: In high terrain, MSL numbers are large. Always convert to AGL and check notes for part-time airspace.

hotspots.title: Sandpoint (SZT)
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Sandpoint is magenta (no tower) with a rotating beacon: elevation 2,131 ft, 5,500 ft lighted runway, CTAF 122.7. The large fuzzy magenta ring around it sets the Class E floor at 700 ft AGL. Area 1, near Sagle, sits at the southern edge of that ring.
hotspots.examTrap: AWOS 135.425 broadcasts weather only. Self-announce on the CTAF, 122.7.

hotspots.title: Coeur d'Alene (COE) Part-Time Class E
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Coeur d'Alene-Boyington is magenta (no tower): elevation 2,320 ft, 7,400 ft lighted runway, CTAF 122.8. Dashed magenta lines show a Class E surface area, and the note "See NOTAMs/Directory for Class E (sfc) eff hrs" means it is only in effect part of the day.
hotspots.examTrap: Check the Chart Supplement for effective hours. Outside those hours, the surface area reverts to the underlying airspace.

hotspots.title: Brooks Seaplane Base (S76)
hotspots.ceiling: Check the COE part-time Class E (sfc) boundary
hotspots.summary: The anchor symbol on Coeur d'Alene Lake is Brooks Seaplane Base: "2125 - 150 122.9" means elevation 2,125 ft, a 15,000 ft water landing lane, and CTAF 122.9. It sits at the south end of the COE dashed magenta boundary, so check whether the part-time surface Class E is in effect.
hotspots.examTrap: For seaplane bases the length figure is the water lane in hundreds of feet: 150 = 15,000 ft.

hotspots.title: Obstruction 4859 (499)
hotspots.summary: West of Coeur d'Alene, an obstruction is charted 4859 (499): top at 4,859 ft MSL, 499 ft above the ground. In mountain terrain the MSL figure looks huge, but the tower itself is just under 500 ft tall.
hotspots.examTrap: Don't treat 4,859 as the tower height. The (499) is height above ground.

hotspots.title: Maximum Elevation Figure 6,600 ft
hotspots.summary: The large blue 6⁶ just south of Magee (S77) is a Maximum Elevation Figure: the highest terrain or obstruction in this latitude/longitude quadrangle, rounded up, is 6,600 ft MSL.
hotspots.examTrap: MEFs are thousands and hundreds of feet MSL, not AGL, and not an airspace floor.

title: Savannah Class C & Bulldog MOAs
subtitle: Class C shelves, MOA exclusions, refuges and untowered fields
keyTakeaway: Savannah's outer Class C shelf starts at 1,300 ft MSL. Read MOA notes carefully for altitude exclusions.

hotspots.title: Savannah/Hilton Head (SAV) Class C Surface
hotspots.summary: The inner magenta ring around Savannah/Hilton Head International is labeled 41/SFC: Class C from the surface to 4,100 ft MSL. Elevation 50 ft, 9,300 ft runway.
hotspots.examTrap: All Class C numbers are MSL. Over a 50 ft field the difference is small, but the principle matters elsewhere.

hotspots.title: Savannah Class C Outer Shelf 41/13
hotspots.summary: Between the inner and outer magenta rings, 41/13 means Class C from 1,300 ft MSL to 4,100 ft MSL. Area 3, north of the Class C, is used in the FAA question about this shelf floor.
hotspots.examTrap: Classic FAA question: the outer shelf floor is 1,300 ft MSL, not 1,300 ft AGL or 1,700 ft MSL.

hotspots.title: Savannah National Wildlife Refuge
hotspots.ceiling: Pilots requested to stay above 2,000 ft AGL
hotspots.summary: Savannah National Wildlife Refuge is labeled northeast of the airport, between the inner and outer Class C rings, so the 41/13 shelf (floor 1,300 ft MSL) is overhead. Pilots are asked to stay above 2,000 ft AGL, which here puts manned aircraft inside Class C.
hotspots.examTrap: A refuge does not replace the airspace around it. Check which Class C ring you are in before deciding on authorization.

hotspots.title: Bulldog B and C MOAs
hotspots.floor: See SUA table; Bulldog C excludes 1,500 ft AGL and below
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: Bulldog B MOA covers this area, and the note "Bulldog C MOA excludes airspace 1500' AGL and below" means the C sector only starts above 1,500 ft AGL. The VR97-1059 military training route crosses here too.
hotspots.examTrap: A MOA needs no authorization, but military jets on low-level routes may be nearby.

hotspots.title: Statesboro-Bulloch County (TBR)
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Statesboro-Bulloch County is magenta (no tower) with a beacon: elevation 187 ft, 6,000 ft lighted runway, CTAF 122.8. A fuzzy magenta ring around it sets Class E at 700 ft AGL. The nearby Statesboro RCO box lists 122.6 for Macon FSS.
hotspots.examTrap: 122.6 in the blue box is the RCO frequency for Flight Service, not the CTAF.

title: Corpus Christi: Class C, Alert Areas, MOAs
subtitle: Student jet training, military Class D and stacked special-use airspace
keyTakeaway: Alert Areas and MOAs need no authorization. Class C surface areas and Class D do.

hotspots.title: Area 3: Corpus Christi Intl Class C Surface
hotspots.summary: Area 3 sits inside the 40/SFC core of the Corpus Christi Class C, next to Corpus Christi International (elevation 44 ft, 7,500 ft runway).
hotspots.examTrap: Inside the SFC ring, authorization is needed from the ground up.

hotspots.title: Corpus Christi Class C Shelf 40/12
hotspots.summary: North of the airport, the outer Class C shelf is labeled 40/12: 1,200 ft MSL to 4,000 ft MSL. Southwest of the field another shelf reads 40/15 (1,500 ft MSL floor).
hotspots.examTrap: Shelf floors differ around the same Class C. Read the label in the segment you are in.

hotspots.title: Area 6: Alert Area A-632C
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: Area 6 is inside Alert Area A-632C, labeled "Concentrated Student Jet Training." Alert areas warn of high-volume pilot training or unusual activity. No permission is needed, but all pilots are equally responsible for collision avoidance.
hotspots.examTrap: Alert Areas are not restricted or prohibited. They are advisories.

hotspots.title: Kingsville NAS (NQI) Class D [25]
hotspots.summary: Kingsville Naval Air Station has a blue airport symbol, a dashed blue Class D ring and [25]: surface to 2,500 ft MSL. Elevation 50 ft, 8,000 ft runway. Area 2 sits just east of the Class D boundary.
hotspots.examTrap: Military airports still use the same Class D rules. [25] is MSL.

hotspots.title: Kingsville 2 MOA
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: Kingsville 2 MOA is labeled south and east of Kingsville NAS. Military aircraft train here; drones may operate without authorization in the underlying Class G but should check MOA activity.
hotspots.examTrap: MOA = no permission needed. R- area = permission needed.

title: Sacramento: Class C, Class D and UAS Notes
subtitle: SMF Class C, Sacramento Executive Class D, parachute and UAS caution notes
keyTakeaway: Busy metro charts stack Class C, Class D and caution notes. Find the boundary you are in before reading any number.

hotspots.title: Sacramento Intl (SMF) Class C Surface
hotspots.summary: The 41/SFC label inside the inner magenta ring means Class C from the surface to 4,100 ft MSL around Sacramento International (elevation 27 ft, 8,600 ft runway).
hotspots.examTrap: Don't mix up SFC rings and shelves when two labels sit close together.

hotspots.title: Sacramento Class C Shelf 41/16
hotspots.summary: Northeast of SMF (note: Figure 71 is oriented with north to the left), the outer shelf reads 41/16: Class C from 1,600 ft MSL to 4,100 ft MSL. Terrain is near sea level, so a 400 ft drone stays well below it.
hotspots.examTrap: The 16 is MSL hundreds: 1,600 ft MSL.

hotspots.title: Area 2: Sacramento Executive (SAC) Class D [25]
hotspots.summary: Area 2 marks Sacramento Executive, a blue part-time towered airport (check star/Chart Supplement for effective hours) with a dashed blue Class D marked [25]: surface to 2,500 ft MSL. Elevation 24 ft, 5,500 ft runway. The SMF Class C outer ring passes just north.
hotspots.examTrap: Each airport has its own boundary. SAC is a Class D, not part of the SMF Class C.

hotspots.title: Area 4: Lincoln Regional (LHM) & Parachute Area
hotspots.summary: Area 4 is next to Lincoln Regional/Harder Field, a magenta untowered airport with a beacon: elevation 121 ft, 6,000 ft lighted runway, CTAF 123.0. The parachute symbol beside it marks a parachute jumping area.
hotspots.examTrap: A parachute symbol means jumpers may be descending through your altitude. Check NOTAMs and the Chart Supplement.

hotspots.title: Caution: Unmanned Aircraft Activity
hotspots.summary: Near Beale AFB the chart boxes read "CAUTION: Unmanned aircraft activity all altitudes," "Intensive flight training in vicinity of BAB 16,500' & below," and a PAVE PAWS radar hazard from the surface to 5,999 ft MSL.
hotspots.examTrap: A caution box is advisory. It does not prohibit flight, but it signals traffic you must see and avoid.

title: Bay Area: Class B over Class C over Class D
subtitle: Livermore Class D, San Jose Class C, restricted R-2531 and a security notice
keyTakeaway: Airspace stacks: San Jose Class C runs to 4,000 MSL with the San Francisco Class B shelf starting at 6,000 MSL above it.

hotspots.title: Area 1: Livermore (LVK) Class D [29]
hotspots.summary: Area 1 is inside the dashed blue Class D around Livermore Municipal, marked [29]: surface to 2,900 ft MSL. Elevation 400 ft, 5,200 ft runway, right-hand traffic for runways 7R and 25R.
hotspots.examTrap: 2,900 MSL over a 400 ft field is 2,500 ft AGL.

hotspots.title: Area 2: Byron (C83)
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Byron is magenta (untowered) with a beacon and a parachute jumping symbol, inside a fuzzy magenta Class E 700 ft AGL ring. CTAF 123.05, right-hand traffic for runways 5 and 30.
hotspots.examTrap: 123.775 is AWOS weather. Use 123.05 for traffic calls.

hotspots.title: Restricted Area R-2531
hotspots.floor: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.ceiling: See SUA table in chart margin
hotspots.summary: The blue hatched polygon east of Livermore is Restricted Area R-2531. Flight inside it while active needs permission from the using or controlling agency.
hotspots.examTrap: LAANC does not cover restricted areas.

hotspots.title: National Security Notice: Avoid 800 ft AGL and Below
hotspots.summary: A magenta NOTICE box reads "For reasons of national security pilots are requested to avoid flight at and below 800' AGL in this area." It covers the hills southeast of Livermore near R-2531.
hotspots.examTrap: This is a request, not a TFR. It still covers every altitude a Part 107 drone can fly.

hotspots.title: Mineta San Jose (SJC) Class C under Class B
hotspots.summary: Mineta San Jose International has a 40/SFC Class C core (surface to 4,000 ft MSL). Elevation 62 ft, 11,000 ft runway. A blue 100/60 label just northwest shows the San Francisco Class B shelf from 6,000 to 10,000 ft MSL above it. Nearby Reid-Hillview has its own Class D [20].
hotspots.examTrap: Above the Class C ceiling you are not automatically in Class E. Here a Class B shelf sits overhead.

title: Sioux City: Obstacles, UC Towers and MTRs
subtitle: Class D math, 2,000 ft towers, under-construction symbols and VR routes
keyTakeaway: Obstacle labels give MSL first and AGL in parentheses. VR routes with three digits have segments above 1,500 ft AGL.

hotspots.title: Sioux Gateway (SUX) Class D [36]
hotspots.summary: Sioux Gateway/Col. Bud Day Field has a dashed blue Class D marked [36]: surface to 3,600 ft MSL. Elevation 1,098 ft, 9,000 ft runway. Dashed magenta lines to the southeast mark a Class E extension toward Salix.
hotspots.examTrap: 3,600 MSL over a 1,098 ft field is about 2,500 ft AGL, not 3,600.

hotspots.title: Lighted Group Obstruction 3370 (2000)
hotspots.summary: Northeast of James, a tall group-obstruction symbol with lightning marks is charted 3370 (2000): 3,370 ft MSL, 2,000 ft above ground, high-intensity lighted. Guy wires can extend far from towers like this.
hotspots.examTrap: The AGL height is in parentheses. Give tall towers a wide berth because of guy wires.

hotspots.title: Pender (0C4) Class E 700 ft Vignette
hotspots.ceiling: Up to but not including 18,000 ft MSL
hotspots.summary: Pender Municipal is magenta with a beacon: elevation 1,345 ft, 3,600 ft lighted runway, CTAF 122.9. The fuzzy magenta circle around it sets the Class E floor at 700 ft AGL.
hotspots.examTrap: No dashed line here, so no surface-area authorization. Class G up to 700 ft AGL.

hotspots.title: Obstruction 1897 (410) UC
hotspots.summary: Near Thurston, an obstruction is charted 1897 (410) UC: top at 1,897 ft MSL, 410 ft above ground, and UC means under construction. It may grow or change before the next chart edition.
hotspots.examTrap: UC = under construction, not "uncontrolled". Check NOTAMs for the current height.

hotspots.title: Military Training Route VR540
hotspots.summary: The gray line labeled VR540 is a VFR Military Training Route. Three-digit route numbers mean one or more segments are above 1,500 ft AGL; four-digit numbers stay at or below 1,500 ft AGL. Military jets fly these routes fast and low.
hotspots.examTrap: VR = VFR route, IR = IFR route. The digit count tells you the altitude band, not the speed.
